articles.title: I already had a VPS, so why was I paying a platform to deploy my apps?
articles.excerpt: I already had my own VPS. It sat there with plenty of RAM, mostly idle. And I was still paying a platform to deploy my apps onto someone else's servers. That felt silly. So I built Dockfin. Platforms…
articles.body: I already had my own VPS. It sat there with plenty of RAM, mostly idle. And I was still paying a platform to deploy my apps onto someone else's servers. That felt silly. So I built Dockfin. The problem nobody puts on the pricing page Platforms like Heroku and Vercel are great at one thing: they make the first deploy feel like magic. You push, you get a URL, you feel like a genius. The trouble starts later. A second app. A database. A preview environment for every pull request. A teammate who needs access. Each of these is reasonable on its own, and together they become a monthly number you try not to look at. The alternative is doing it yourself. Docker, a reverse proxy, TLS, webhooks, backups, all wired up by hand. That's a weekend you never get back, and then you have to maintain it.
articles.author: Foisal Islam

articles.title: Five Retention Numbers in Our Own API: What /api/auth/config Publishes About Your Data
articles.excerpt: I work on OnePassApps, so this is our own product, and every number below was read from our live API and our live legal page in one session on 4 November 2026. Our privacy copy is careful. It tells yo…
articles.body: I work on OnePassApps, so this is our own product, and every number below was read from our live API and our live legal page in one session on 4 November 2026. Our privacy copy is careful. It tells you what we keep, where we keep it, and it gives you a way to ask. In most places it deliberately does not print the retention period itself - "Contact us for the current backup period and the status of a deletion request." The API is more direct. One public route, no account and no session, answers with our privacy configuration - including five retention numbers - in plain JSON. This is what it returns, and how it lines up with the words on the terms page. The route GET https://api.onepassapps.com/api/auth/config That is the whole request: no key, no cookie, no session.

articles.title: Self-Hosting a CMS: Control, Costs, and Operational Risks
articles.excerpt: Self-hosting a CMS means deploying it in infrastructure you choose and operate directly or through a provider. That infrastructure might be a virtual server, shared hosting, a managed environment, or…
articles.body: Self-hosting a CMS means deploying it in infrastructure you choose and operate directly or through a provider. That infrastructure might be a virtual server, shared hosting, a managed environment, or equipment your organization owns. “Self-hosted” describes the deployment model; it does not mean the physical server has to be in your office. The appeal is control over the environment, data access, and integration choices. The tradeoff is operational responsibility. Before choosing a deployment model, decide who will patch it, monitor it, restore it, and respond when something breaks. Hosting, management, and licensing are separate choices A self-hosted CMS can use an open-source or commercial license. Conversely, a managed service may build on open-source software.

articles.body: La Quest 2 s'éteint : concevoir un visualiseur PDB VR indépendant du matériel Quand Meta a annoncé la fin du support de la Quest 2, mon premier réflexe n'a pas été la nostalgie. Ça a été : combien de codeurs dans mon labo vont se retrouver avec un casque orphelin ? On avait passé deux ans à prototyper un visualiseur de structures protéiques en VR, et voilà que la plateforme sous nos pieds se dérobait. J'ai repensé à ce soir de novembre, dans le bureau mal éclairé du troisième étage, quand Sarah — doctorante en bio-informatique — avait arraché son casque en soupirant : « Je vois rien, c'est flou, et j'ai mal au crâne. » Elle venait de passer trois heures sur une protéine membranaire, à essayer de comprendre comment un ligand se glissait dans une poche hydrophobe.

articles.title: SMS-Based OTP Authentication Explained — Third-Party APIs for Support Queue Evidence
articles.excerpt: A customer-support team using third-party APIs to implement SMS-based OTP needs evidence before routing a contact form as authenticated. The Node.js integration must connect the authentication decisio…
articles.body: A customer-support team using third-party APIs to implement SMS-based OTP needs evidence before routing a contact form as authenticated. The Node.js integration must connect the authentication decision to the right submission. A message delivery receipt cannot carry that argument by itself. Short answer: implement SMS-based OTP in Node.js through a third-party API, with separate steps for sending a challenge and verifying the submitted code. For two-factor authentication, bind that challenge to an existing first-factor session. Release the contact form to its support queue only after the backend records a successful verification for that session and submission. Choose a provider whose evidence your compliance review can actually use. Keep the boundary small.

articles.title: NASA's Swift space telescope crashes back to Earth after failed rescue attempt
articles.excerpt: NASA's Swift space telescope crashed back to Earth today (Nov. 4), three months after a private spacecraft was supposed to boost the observatory to a higher orbit.
articles.body: NASA's Swift space telescope has reached the end of its long and winding road. Swift fell uncontrolled to Earth today (Nov. 4), 22 years after it launched but just three months after a private spacecraft was supposed to boost it to a higher, life-extending orbit. The 3,200-pound (1,450 kilograms) observatory reentered Earth's atmosphere at 7:39 a.m. EST (1239 GMT) today over northern Sumatra, according to satellite tracker Jonathan McDowell , who cited U.S. Space Force data. The fall likely didn't make much of an impact; NASA officials predicted beforehand that most of the minibus-sized Swift would burn up as it fell, and they put the odds of any of the surviving pieces hurting anyone on Earth at just 1 in 2,100.

articles.title: Mars isn't dead — recent volcanic activity reveals it's just sleeping
articles.excerpt: Scientists have long suspected that Mars is geologically "dead" but new spacecraft observations suggests the Red Planet's volcanoes are merely sleeping.
articles.body: Scientists have long suspected that Mars is geologically "dead," but new spacecraft observations suggest the Red Planet's volcanoes are merely sleeping. That means that Olympus Mons , the extinct Martian volcano that at around 16 miles (26 kilometers) above the surrounding Martian plains is the largest mountain in the solar system , may in fact be a slumbering giant. The observations were made with the European Space Agency (ESA) mission ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO) as it studied volcanic fissures along the Alba Mons region of the Red Planet. Alba Mons is in the Tharsis region of Mars, the same area that is home to Olympus Mons.

articles.title: NASA's Artemis II moon launch tore a hole in Earth's upper atmosphere so huge it disrupted GPS signals
articles.excerpt: "It could have a strong impact not only on self-driving cars but also on drone positioning."
articles.body: The launch of NASA's Artemis II mission in April 2026 caused significant disturbances in Earth's ionosphere that could have triggered temporary, localized errors in GPS positioning, a new study has found. The study, by a team of researchers from National Cheng Kung University in Taiwan, analyzed data from high-precision networks of fixed, ground-based GPS receivers, used by U.S. scientific institutions to measure the minuscule motions of Earth's tectonic plates in the lead-up to earthquakes.
